\label{fig:margin}

Our pre-specified test of whether aggregate agreement hides them (H1: aggregate agreement is high and the decision-level share at least ten points lower) uses, per cell, the contrast between the mean Pearson correlation and the share with $P_c^{\varepsilon}\ge0.9$ (Table~\ref{tab:h1}).
Read with the tolerance, it is not supported at a default or reference budget: the contrast is within $0.1$ points of zero in every cell, as it must be where $P_c^{\varepsilon}$ forgives near-tie swaps.
Read strictly, with $P_c\ge0.9$ in place of $P_c^{\varepsilon}\ge0.9$, the contrast at the reference budget is $3$ to $21$ points for the non-linear models; it reaches the ten points in the random forests on Pima ($13.0$, interval $7.0$--$19.0$) and GMSC ($21.0$, $13.0$--$29.0$) and its interval excludes zero in $9$ of the $15$ cells.
The counts below, again with the tolerance, are for the \texttt{shap} Kernel explainer; the paired Kernel estimator at equal budgets holds it in $72$ of the $84$ non-linear cells.
It holds, with a bootstrap interval excluding zero, in every cell at budgets of about $2d$ and below ($m=32$ for German Credit and ACS Employment, $m=13$ for Pima: contrasts of $40$--$90$ points), and above that in $7$ of $93$ non-linear cells at budgets of at least $3d$: German Credit at $m=64$ for the random forest, boosting and the MLP ($16$--$33$ points), ACS Employment random forest at $m=64$, random forests on ACS Income and GMSC at $m=51$, and boosting on Pima at $m=25$.
At every budget of at least $3d$ the mean Pearson correlation of the \texttt{shap} Kernel explainer is at least $0.97$.

\subsection{Budget, estimators and the margin law}
\label{sec:budget}
The error of $\hat\phi$ falls with $m$ at a rate that depends on the estimator (Figure~\ref{fig:budget}a).
For the paired Kernel and antithetic permutation estimators the log--log slope of the relative $L_2$ error is $-0.49$ to $-0.53$ on every non-linear cell, as sampling theory says; the \texttt{shap} Kernel explainer falls faster, with slopes of $-0.62$ to $-0.66$ on the two larger datasets and $-0.76$ to $-0.91$ on the $d\le10$ ones, while with \texttt{num\_features(10)} the error hardly falls (slope $-0.02$ to $-0.17$) because the estimator is biased.
At equal numbers of model evaluations neither of our estimators beats the unchanged default (Figure~\ref{fig:budget}b): the paired Kernel estimator has a lower share of exact instances by $0.19$--$0.38$ and a lower tolerance-aware share by $0.04$--$0.10$ in all six non-linear cells of the two larger datasets, beyond the smallest resolvable difference, and antithetic permutation is indistinguishable from the default (differences $-0.015$ to $+0.001$ in the strict share, none beyond the smallest resolvable difference).

shown.message:
I changed the H1 sentences in §5.3 to match what `h1_contrast.csv` computes. The head of #11 (`candidate-v2` into `main`) is now 79b0a4a. In the system build the main text still ends on page 9, and there are no Type 3 fonts.

- **Small budgets:** at m=32 (German Credit, ACS Employment) and m=13 (Pima) the contrast is 45–90 points. The mean Pearson correlation is itself below 0.9 in 8 of the 9 non-linear cells, so the aggregate is not high there. H1 holds only for the Pima MLP.
- **Budgets of at least 3d:** H1 holds in 7 of 93 non-linear cells, as before.
- **Paired Kernel estimator:** H1 holds in 29 of 84 non-linear cells, not 72. The 72 is the number of cells where the decision-level share is at least ten points below the mean Pearson, without the aggregate-high condition. I kept it as a parenthetical.
- **Discussion:** the sentence now says high aggregate agreement hides failures "in a minority of cells at small budgets".

I asked `experiment-repo` in the PR thread to re-check lines 44–46 of `paper/results.tex`. `figtab-repo`'s review of #11 and the Arrhythmia results are still pending.
